summary.short: 21 CFR § 882.1491 defines a pediatric Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis aid as a prescription device and classifies it as Class II (special controls). The special controls require clinical performance testing, software and cybersecurity documentation, usability assessment, and specified labeling. No effective date is stated.
summary.long: The rule is an administrative classification under 21 CFR § 882.1491 for a device intended as an aid in diagnosing Autism Spectrum Disorder in pediatric patients. It is placed in Class II (special controls). Under paragraph (b), the special controls require: clinical performance testing against a reference method of diagnosis, including sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values; software verification, validation and hazard analysis, with a technical description of the algorithms and a cybersecurity assessment; a usability assessment showing intended users can safely and correctly use the device; and labeling with instructions for use, a summary of clinical testing, and a statement that the device is not intended as a stand-alone diagnostic. The text states no effective date and contains no enforcement provisions or penalties.
